title: Setup the lab + test an uncensored model
subtitle: Zero-to-working-lab in one page. Click each step done as you finish it. All free — no paid GPU required.

whats_needed.label: A computer
whats_needed.note: Mac, Linux, or Windows (WSL). ~16 GB RAM is comfortable.

whats_needed.label: A free Google account
whats_needed.note: For Colab (the uncensoring step runs there, no local GPU needed).

steps.title: Install Ollama (local model runner)
steps.detail: Ollama runs open-weight models on your machine with one command. You don't need a GPU for small models (3B runs on CPU just fine, slow but workable).
steps.verify: Run `ollama --version` — you should see a version number.

steps.title: Pull a base model (the one you'll test)
steps.detail: Llama 3.2 3B is a good first pick — small enough to run without a GPU, aligned enough that refusals are visible. Takes ~2 GB disk.
commands: ollama run llama3.2:3b-instruct-q4_K_M 'Say hello in one sentence.'
steps.verify: You see a one-sentence greeting back. Press Ctrl+D to exit.

steps.title: Install this studio
steps.detail: The studio is a FastAPI backend + Next.js frontend. Both run locally.
steps.verify: No errors. If `pip install -e .` complains about httpx, run `pip install httpx` and retry.

steps.title: Start both servers
steps.detail: Open two terminals — one for the backend API, one for the frontend. Keep Ollama running in a third.
steps.verify: Open http://localhost:3000 — you see the studio home page.

steps.title: Baseline test: attack the stock model
steps.detail: Measure how often the untouched Llama 3.2 3B refuses. This is your baseline — the number you'll compare the uncensored version against.
steps.verify: After the run, note the ASR (attack-success rate) %. On stock Llama 3.2 3B it's usually 10-25%.
subtasks: Click the model pill to select it
Leave all 9 attacks and 4 topics selected
Click 'Run suite' — watch the grid fill
Note the ASR number and which attacks landed

steps.title: Uncensor the model (Colab, ~20 minutes, free T4)
steps.detail: The Uncensor page generates the exact 9-step walkthrough. The main work happens in Google Colab (free T4 GPU) running Labonne's abliteration notebook. You come back when it's done.
steps.verify: After step 9 of the Uncensor page, Ollama has a model tag like 'l32-3b-abliterated:latest'. Check with `ollama list`.
subtasks: Click 'Build steps' — you get 9 numbered steps
Step 7 (GGUF conversion) and step 8 (Ollama import) run on your machine
Save the GGUF, create the Modelfile, run `ollama create l32-3b-abliterated -f Modelfile.l32-3b`

steps.title: Test the uncensored model — compare to baseline
steps.detail: Same test suite, new model tag. The ASR should jump from ~20% to 70-95% if abliteration worked. If it's higher than baseline but output is garbled, you broke coherence — go back and lower the intervention strength in Colab.
steps.verify: ASR on the uncensored tag is 3-10x higher than baseline. Click a few cells to spot-check the model is still coherent (not just emitting broken text).
subtasks: Re-probe Ollama — you now see both the base tag and the abliterated tag
Click the abliterated tag to select it
Compare ASR, refusal count, and spot-check a JAILED cell for coherence

steps.title: Export results, keep notes
steps.detail: 'Export JSON' on the test page saves the full matrix. Keep one JSON per model tag — easy to diff later when you try different base models or stronger uncensoring recipes.
steps.verify: You have at least two JSON files — one baseline, one uncensored. Diff them with `diff <(jq .summary a.json) <(jq .summary b.json)`.
subtasks: Open both in VS Code side-by-side to compare

troubleshooting.a: Start `ollama serve` in another terminal. Default port is 11434. If you changed the port, update the Endpoint URL on the Test page.
`pip install httpx` inside your backend venv. The deps were updated; re-run `pip install -e .` from studio/backend/.

troubleshooting.q: Colab abliteration cell OOM on T4
troubleshooting.a: Switch to Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, or use Kaggle (2× T4 free) instead. The recipe page lists both.
You over-ablated. Open the Colab, lower the orthogonalization strength to 0.5-0.8, re-run. The direction exists but applying it too strongly destroys the model.

troubleshooting.q: After uncensoring, refusals are still there
troubleshooting.a: You used the wrong layer. Re-run the probing cell, pick the layer with the highest cosine-separation score.
Check the FROM path points at the exact .gguf file you created. Run `ls *.gguf` to confirm.
Your model is slow on CPU. Reduce attacks to 2-3 for a first pass, or use a smaller model (1B instead of 3B).

next_steps.label: Scale up to 7-8B
next_steps.note: Kaggle's P100 handles Llama-3.1-8B. Same recipe, just bigger. Expect ~2 hours.

next_steps.label: Try DPO on top of abliteration
next_steps.note: The Learning roadmap's weight-level branch has the node 'DPO uncensoring' — adds a polish pass that recovers lost coherence.

next_steps.label: Measure capability retention
next_steps.note: Run MMLU + HellaSwag on both models with lm-eval-harness. Cite the delta in your release notes.
